title: Vintage Fender Precision Bass Value Guide: 1951 To 1979
description: Vintage Fender Precision Bass values for 1951 to 1979, with annual rows, slab-body and gold-guard comparisons, condition notes and photos from my archive.
h1: Vintage Fender Precision Bass Value Guide
alt: Early blonde Fender Precision Bass beside a tweed Bassman amplifier

faqs.q: How Much Is A Vintage Fender Precision Bass Worth?
faqs.a: As of October 2026, the guide ranges span $2,100 to $40,000, with exceptional early examples potentially exceeding that range. Original 1951 to 1953 slab-body basses sit at $20,000 to $40,000 or more. The late-1970s range is $2,100 to $4,000 under the stated condition assumptions.

faqs.q: What Is A 1952 Fender Precision Bass Worth?
faqs.a: The 1951 to 1953 range is $20,000 to $40,000 or more for all-original examples in Very Good to Excellent condition. Modified player examples have a separate $8,000 to $15,000 range. Neither includes an accompanying amplifier; substantial changes need an individual appraisal.

faqs.q: What Is A 1978 Fender Precision Bass Worth?
faqs.a: The shared 1975 to 1979 standard-finish comparison is $2,100 to $4,000. It assumes original finish and pickup, with the disclosed allowances for wear, serviced wiring, missing accessories and case condition. Refinishes, routing and replacement pickups need different comparisons.

faqs.q: Why Do Some Years Share A Price Range?
faqs.a: Adjacent years can share an era range. I assess the exact construction and condition before narrowing it. The condition notes explain which instruments each band covers.

faqs.q: Does A Quality Refret Change The Originality Category?
faqs.a: A quality refret is accepted maintenance and preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise all-original bass. It takes the instrument out of the museum-quality category. Neck reshaping and substantial fingerboard alterations are separate changes.

faqs.q: Does A Refinish Have A Fixed Percentage Deduction?
faqs.a: No. A refinish changes the collector comparison, but the year, retained parts, structural condition and quality of the work still need to be assessed. I don't use one percentage for every modified bass.

faqs.q: Is A Dealer Offer The Same As The Guide Range?
faqs.a: No. The guide is a market comparison with stated conditions. An offer has its own terms, included accessories and responsibilities. Private-sale proceeds also depend on fees, shipping and the final agreement.

faqs.q: Should I Replace Parts Before An Appraisal?
faqs.a: Start by documenting the bass as it is. Keep removed parts, photographs and repair records together. I don't need cosmetic restoration or unfamiliar disassembly before an initial appraisal.
